kinds.d: Cluster of tubes linked by one fuse that fires a timed series of aerial effects.
t: Peony, willow, palm, crossette, crackle effects

kinds.d: Firework driven upward by its own solid-fuel motor, steadied by a stick or fins, that bursts near the top of its climb.

x.d: Small, cheap black-powder skyrocket on a thin bamboo splint, often sold by the pack or gross.
Rocket that burns whistle mix instead of black powder, screaming as it climbs.

kinds.d: Shell fired from a mortar tube that bursts high in the air into a patterned break of stars.

x.d: Spherical burst of coloured stars without tails; the most common shell type.
Spherical burst of coloured stars that leave visible spark trails.
Spherical burst with fewer, larger stars that travel farther.
Chrysanthemum with long-burning silver or gold stars that droop into a dome.
Chrysanthemum of dense glittering silver or gold stars with a heavy glitter trail.
A few large comet stars with a thick rising tail, like a palm tree.
Large stars that split into smaller stars in a criss-cross pattern.
Directional burst of heavy tailed stars falling a short way.
Stars bursting in a circle; variants form hearts or smiley faces.
Fast-burning tailed stars forming radial lines like spider legs.
Stars that dart rapidly away from the burst.
Large, slow-burning stars that leave glittering, sizzling sparks.
Quick flash of flash powder followed by a loud report.

kinds.d: Long tube that fires stars or small shells one after another at regular intervals.
Mortar-launched canister that throws all its stars and effects upward at once.
Ground firework that throws up a cone of sparks.
Spinning firework on a pin, driven by a powder-filled spiral tube or angled rockets.
Small firework that spins on the ground throwing a circle of sparks.
Small paper-cased explosive with a fuse, made mainly for a loud bang.

x.d: Strings of small black-powder crackers, mostly red, braided to fire in sequence.
x.dt: string length · red with a few yellow or green

x.d: Cracker filled with flash powder for a sharper, brighter bang.
Round red salute with a green fuse like a cherry stem; full-power versions banned for US consumers in 1966.
Tiny paper twist of gravel and a trace of silver fulminate that pops when thrown.

kinds.a: smoke bomb · coloured smoke · smoke grenade
kinds.d: Firework that releases a large volume of coloured or white smoke.
Hand-held wire coated with a slow-burning pyrotechnic that throws sparks.

x.d: Thin metal wire, about 20–30 cm, dipped in metal-fuel composition; the fuel sets the spark colour.
x.dt: length · aluminium, iron, titanium or ferrotitanium sparks

x.d: Twisted tissue-paper stick about 20 cm long tipped with a few grains of black powder, giving fine branching sparks.

brands.d: Fireworks brand known for award-winning cake and compound effects, sold widely in the UK.
Huddersfield firework maker founded by James Greenhalgh; UK production ended in 1998 and the name is now a Black Cat brand.
Oldest British firework maker, founded by John Brock in Islington; bought by Standard Fireworks in 1988.
China-based fireworks company that bought Standard Fireworks in 1998 and trades in the UK under several names.
Germany's largest consumer fireworks maker, based in Eitorf.

traditions.d: China's main centre of firework and firecracker making for over 1,400 years, exporting since 1875.
traditions.tech: hand and factory filling of paper-cased crackers and shells
traditions.auth: Liuyang fireworks are a protected origin product

notes: Old 'Other fireworks' dissolved: Brothers/Evo/Primed/Pyroworx items into Firework cake (planner says mostly cakes; Bangalangers type unconfirmed), Space X moved to Firework rocket (retailer lists it as a rocket). Effect types (peony…salute) are archetypes of Aerial shell, sourced to Wikipedia Fireworks, and appear as t on cakes; strobe not attested so left out. Dept brief suggestion: classes EU F1–F4 (F2 sold to over-18s; F3/F4 not to consumers in Germany), UK Categories 1–4 (Cat 1 16+, Cat 2–3 18+, Cat 4 professionals only) per Wikipedia Fireworks; US consumer class 1.4G is from knowledge — to verify. Brands left out: Epic Fireworks (only a search snippet: Batley showroom), Zena (nothing found), Cobra (Cobra Firing Systems is a firing-system maker, not a firework brand; a 'Firing system' kind could be added if wanted). Black Cat Fireworks Wikipedia title redirects to Li & Fung, so Black Cat cites the Standard Fireworks page. No versions added: none confirmed. Liuyang added as a tradition; Japanese hanabi tradition not added (no source retrieved).
